sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
# Generative AI / LLM / Agentic AI Engineer Interview Playbook (300 Questions)

This playbook is designed for interview preparation at top AI product companies and research-driven engineering teams. It covers scenario debugging, RAG, agentic systems, MCP, LLM internals, prompt engineering, and system design.

sections.title: Distribution
sections.body:
- Scenario-Based Generative AI Problems: 120
- Agentic AI Systems: 60
- RAG Systems: 50
- Model Context Protocol (MCP): 20
- LLM Internals and Fine-Tuning: 25
- Prompt Engineering: 15
- Generative AI System Design: 10
- Total: 300

sections.title: Q1 [Scenario]
sections.body:
### 1. Question
Scenario: In production, RAG returns wrong answers despite correct source docs. How do you identify root cause, debug quickly, and apply durable architecture fixes?

### 2. Answer
Start with incident containment and observability, then isolate which layer regressed and apply a targeted fix validated by replay and canary rollout.

### 3. Detailed Explanation
Root cause analysis: Retriever recall is low because chunk IDs or metadata filters exclude relevant documents. Debugging steps: Replay failing query with trace IDs, inspect top-k docs, and compute recall@k on golden questions. Architecture fixes: Add query rewriting, metadata guardrails, and reranking with grounded answer constraints.

### 4. Example Implementation (Python when applicable)
```python
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()

resp = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-4.1",
    input="Answer only from retrieved context",
    temperature=0.2
)
print(resp.output_text)
```

### 5. Production Best Practices
Maintain end-to-end traces per request, track groundedness and retrieval quality KPIs, deploy with canary + rollback, cache stable retrieval results, and separate latency budget across retrieval, generation, and tools.

### 6. Common Interview Pitfalls
Candidates often jump straight to prompt tweaks, ignore instrumentation, skip failure segmentation, and fail to mention experiment design, rollback strategy, or measurable SLO/SLA impact.
